results.reason: Issue 1 quotes MSA § 3.2's nationwide exclusivity covering all warehousing, freight and delivery, contrasts it with Term Sheet § 4.1's NYC-metro last-mile scope, and proposes replacement language tracking the Term Sheet.

Issue 2 explains that § 11.3 carves Customer's § 10.2 indemnity out of the cap and the consequential-damages exclusion while Bellweather's § 10.1 indemnity stays capped. It calls this one-sided unlimited exposure and recommends deleting the carve-out or making it mutual.
Issue 3 identifies DPA § 9.1's Delaware law and Wilmington courts, states that the DPA prevails under MSA § 2.3, and recommends conforming the DPA to MSA § 18 (New York).
Issue 4 identifies the 3-year auto-renewals and the 15-day notice window in § 14.2, explains the lock-in risk, and recommends 1-year renewals with a 90-day notice period.
The response never addresses SOW § 8.2 provider assignment without consent or the one-sided MSA § 17.4 assignment clause.
The response quotes § 2.3: 'the Data Processing Addendum, then this Agreement, then the Statement of Work'.
The response states that the § 11.1 cap is 'the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim'.
The response is a MEMORANDUM to the Supervising Partner, and each issue gives the Where, Why it matters (or the problem), and a Recommended fix.
The issues are expressly ordered by importance, and Part IV lists items to raise with the client before the next turn of the draft.
The response concludes that the DPA's Delaware clause controls data disputes and that the two documents conflict.
The response states that the exclusivity clause is far broader than the Term Sheet scope.
